description:
Gothenburg Museum of Art holds European and American art from the fifteenth century to the present, with a strong emphasis on Nordic art. The Fürstenberg Gallery is an important part of its historical collection.

Nordic art around 1900, the Gothenburg Colourists, French painting and international modernism connect different strands of the museum’s holdings. Contemporary Nordic work extends the collection into more recent practice.

description:
The Hallwyl Museum preserves the Stockholm home and collections of Wilhelmina and Walther von Hallwyl. The late nineteenth-century house became a public museum in 1938.

Art, antiques and domestic interiors reveal the interests of an extensive collector and the world in which the family lived. Changing exhibitions offer additional perspectives on the historic house and its contents.

description:
Helsingborg Museum is a municipal museum whose activities extend across the city. Its sites and exhibitions explore local history, cultural heritage and art, including work at Dunkers Kulturhus.

Its art collection ranges across painting, prints, photography, sculpture and other media, with particular connections to Helsingborg and northwestern Skåne. The collection store and public exhibition venues have different functions.

description:
Kulturmagasinet at Fredriksdal in Helsingborg is a centre for museum collections, archives and conservation. Its facilities support the documentation, care and storage of objects belonging to the city’s museums.

description:
Millesgården on Lidingö was created by sculptor Carl Milles and painter Olga Milles. It combines their former home and studios with a terraced sculpture park and an exhibition gallery.

Sculptures and fountains connect the gardens with views over Stockholm’s inlet. Changing exhibitions and Anne’s House, furnished by Estrid Ericson and Josef Frank, add further perspectives on art and design.

description:
Prince Eugen’s Waldemarsudde in Stockholm combines an artist’s former home, art collections and gardens. Prince Eugen was a landscape painter and a collector closely engaged with the art of his time.

Swedish painting forms the core of the collection, alongside sculpture, drawings and prints. Works by artists of his own generation and early modernists connect the house with wider Nordic artistic developments.

description:
The Maritime Museum and Aquarium in Gothenburg explores life on, above and below the sea. Maritime history and marine science provide complementary approaches to the relationship between people and water.

Its collections include ship models, designs, photographs, archives and objects associated especially with merchant shipping. The collections developed from the activities of Gothenburg’s Nautical Society in the nineteenth century.

description:
The Archaeological Museum at Nagarjunakonda preserves material recovered from the valley before the creation of the Nagarjuna Sagar reservoir. The island museum is approached from Vijayapuri South.

Buddhist sculpture, inscriptions, relic caskets and other antiquities illuminate the region’s religious and artistic history. Earlier archaeological material broadens the account beyond its major early historic monuments.

Sculpture, paintings, coins and other material provide different perspectives on Goa’s past. This Archaeological Survey of India museum is distinct from the Goa State Museum in Panaji.
